columns.name: Tokens
columns.desc: Tokens seen in the main pretraining stage. Inherited values (italic) belong to the base model the recipe started from.

columns.name: Data mix
columns.desc: The headline of the pretraining mixture: proportions where the lab gives them, the corpus name otherwise.

columns.name: Anneal / CPT
columns.desc: Tokens in a separate stage between pretraining and post-training: a learning-rate anneal on a curated mix, a reasoning stage, or continued pretraining on a domain.

columns.name: Context
columns.desc: Final trained context length, and how it was reached (stages, tokens, RoPE scaling).

columns.name: SFT
columns.desc: Supervised fine-tuning set size in examples (prompts or annotations). Rows that give only tokens show them but sort with the undisclosed.

columns.name: Preference
columns.desc: Preference stage: method (reward model, DPO, APO, QRPO) and the size of its data.

columns.name: RL
columns.desc: Reinforcement learning: algorithm and number of distinct prompts or problems.

columns.name: Distillation
columns.desc: Learning from a teacher model: logit distillation, teacher-written SFT data (sequence level), or serving as the teacher.

columns.name: As disclosed
columns.desc: Compute as the lab states it. Sorts by GPU-hours of whatever accelerator was used (A100, H100, H800, GH200 are not equal); rows that give only FLOPs, energy or dollars sort with the undisclosed.

columns.name: 6ND
columns.desc: Pretraining FLOPs by the 6 x active parameters x tokens rule, the same yardstick for every row. Derived here unless the paper prints it.

columns.name: Weights
columns.desc: Weights licence: 2 = OSI-style open (Apache 2.0, MIT), 1 = custom open-weights licence, 0 = closed.

columns.name: Data
columns.desc: Training data: 2 = released, 1 = partly released, 0 = not released.

columns.name: Code
columns.desc: Code: 2 = training code released, 1 = inference or partial, 0 = none.

report.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

pt_tokens.note: 1M steps at a batch of 2^11 sequences of 512 tokens; exactly 2^40 = 1.10T if the million steps are 2^20. The ablation baseline saw only 2^35, about 34B tokens.

pt_mix.note: C4 is about 750 GB of English from one month of Common Crawl (April 2019), cleaned with heuristics. The final models mix the supervised tasks into pretraining (C4 given an artificial size of 133M examples for the 11B).

mid_tokens.note: No separate annealing or mid-training stage; the multi-task mix runs through pretraining.

ctx.note: Sequences of 512 tokens with relative position buckets; no long-context stage.

sft.m: GLUE, SuperGLUE etc., task by task
sft.note: Supervised fine-tuning on each benchmark separately (batch 8), not instruction or chat tuning; no example count for the whole stage.

pref.note: Predates preference tuning: the recipe is pretraining then supervised fine-tuning.

compute.note: Trained on Cloud TPU Pods; no hours, chips-days or FLOPs are given for the final models.

c6nd.note: 6ND assumes a decoder-only model where every parameter sees every token; for an encoder-decoder each token passes through roughly half the parameters, so the rule is not applied here.

d_open.note: Released as a TensorFlow Datasets build from Common Crawl; Ai2 later hosted the processed files (allenai/c4).

report.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

pt_mix.note: Weights in the training mix, not shares of available data: Common Crawl is 82% of the tokens available but 60% of the mix; Wikipedia is seen 3.4 times.

mid_tokens.note: No annealing stage; PPO-ptx mixes pretraining gradients into RL instead.

sft.note: 11,295 labeler-written plus 1,430 customer prompts (train split). The text rounds to "about 13k".

pref.m: 6B reward model on rankings of 4 to 9 answers
pref.note: Each prompt carries 4 to 9 ranked answers, so the comparisons number several per prompt (up to C(9,2) = 36). Not DPO: a reward model trained for the RL step.

rl.note: 256K episodes over about 31K unique customer prompts; pretraining gradients mixed in (ptx) to cut the alignment tax.

compute.note: Post-training is 64.9 of 3,704.9 petaflop/s-days, 1.75% of the whole; the paper quotes PPO-ptx alone against pretraining (60 / 3,640 = 1.6%).

d_open.note: Prompts came from OpenAI API customers and labelers; not published.
